meta.title: The 529 Network Social Fact Bank
meta.governance: One approved wording and one source location per statistic. National findings are distinct from state-specific rules. The 529 Network is the data source; ISS is downstream. No ranking or best-plan language.
known_discrepancies: Tax savings: p.42 states $439M (APPROVED for social use); p.7 summary states $413M. Do not mix.

campaign_findings.headline: $275M
campaign_findings.approved_statement: State 529 plans and their partners invest almost $275 million directly into 529 accounts to help families save for education.
campaign_findings.qualifier: National topline. Combines several program types across states.
campaign_findings.notes: Headline invest figure; component non-tax incentives round to about $220M.

campaign_findings.headline: $439M+
campaign_findings.approved_statement: 529 participation is tied to more than $439 million in state tax savings, through personal income tax deductions and credits.
campaign_findings.qualifier: Tax benefits differ by state; seven states have no personal income tax. Conservative estimate (report endnote 10).
campaign_findings.notes: Approved topline set to $439M per Ahmed/Catherine. Summary p.7 states $413M for the same measure; retained as a known variant, not for social use.

campaign_findings.headline: $220.6M
campaign_findings.approved_statement: In 2024, state plans and their partners invested $220.6 million in financial incentives for opening and contributing to 529 accounts.
campaign_findings.qualifier: National topline. Includes matching grants, initial contributions, and other direct incentives.
campaign_findings.notes: p.7 summary rounds to $220M non-tax incentives.

campaign_findings.headline: 12 states / $21.4M
campaign_findings.approved_statement: Twelve states offer matching-grant programs, investing $21.4 million to match family contributions in 2024.
campaign_findings.qualifier: Match rates, caps, and eligibility differ by state.
campaign_findings.notes: Seven states use 1:1; five use other methods.

campaign_findings.headline: 11 states
campaign_findings.approved_statement: Eleven states provide initial contributions that help start a 529 account, some automatically for children born or entering school in the state.
campaign_findings.qualifier: Programs, amounts, and eligibility differ by state.

campaign_findings.headline: 41 states
campaign_findings.approved_statement: Forty-one states have a minimum initial contribution of $25 or less to open a 529 account, and many have no minimum at all.
campaign_findings.qualifier: Minimums differ by state; some advisor-sold plans have higher minimums.
campaign_findings.notes: Strategy anchor fact for the atomization example.

campaign_findings.approved_statement: 34 states report targeted rural outreach, 32 accept ITINs as account-owner identification, and 23 provide plan information in Spanish.
campaign_findings.qualifier: Availability and services differ by state.
campaign_findings.notes: Spanish figure is 23 of responding states.

campaign_findings.headline: 27 states
campaign_findings.approved_statement: A majority of responding states (27) provide financial education for current and prospective 529 account owners.

campaign_findings.headline: 17 states / $21M
campaign_findings.approved_statement: Seventeen states reported college-access partnerships; where savings data are available, those 529 accounts held more than $21 million.
campaign_findings.qualifier: Partnership models differ by state; savings outcomes are not always reported.

campaign_findings.headline: 18 states
campaign_findings.approved_statement: Eighteen states reported local savings partnerships, identifying at least 32 partnerships and more than $4.1 million in incentives in 2024.
campaign_findings.qualifier: Conservative estimate; based on limited survey responses.

campaign_findings.headline: $28.8M
campaign_findings.approved_statement: State 529 plans awarded more than $28.8 million in higher-education scholarships in 2024.
campaign_findings.qualifier: Scholarship programs and eligibility differ by state.

campaign_findings.headline: 9 states
campaign_findings.approved_statement: Nine states provide a tax credit or deduction for employers that contribute to employees' 529 accounts.
campaign_findings.qualifier: Employer benefit rules differ by state; total employer credits were about $429,000 in 2024.

state_spotlights.headline: $2.2B / 5M accounts
state_spotlights.approved_statement: California's CalKIDS automatically seeds a 529 account for every newborn and eligible public-school student; more than 5 million accounts held nearly $2.2 billion in assets as of June 2025.
state_spotlights.qualifier: Eligibility and deposit amounts are state-specific.

state_spotlights.headline: 672,000 accounts / $67M
state_spotlights.approved_statement: Pennsylvania's Keystone Scholars gives every newborn a $100 starter deposit; more than 672,000 accounts were funded, totaling over $67 million as of June 2024.
state_spotlights.qualifier: Funded by surplus investment earnings, not taxpayer funds. State-specific.

state_spotlights.headline: 4:1 match
state_spotlights.approved_statement: Tennessee's TIPS program matches qualifying contributions 4:1 for eligible lower-income households, up to $500 per year.
state_spotlights.qualifier: Income eligibility is state-specific; lifetime cap of $1,500.

state_spotlights.headline: $90M / 180,000 children
state_spotlights.approved_statement: Maine gives every resident newborn a $500 Alfond Grant; the program has invested over $90 million for more than 180,000 children since 2013.
state_spotlights.qualifier: State-specific; first statewide CSA program in the nation.

state_spotlights.headline: 14,000 accounts / $19M
state_spotlights.approved_statement: Virginia's SOAR Virginia pairs early-commitment advising and financial literacy with scholarship funds held in 529 accounts; it has opened 14,000 accounts holding $19 million.
state_spotlights.qualifier: Eligibility and pledge requirements are state-specific.

state_spotlights.headline: 274,000 accounts / $50M+
state_spotlights.approved_statement: New York's NYC Kids RISE, the largest local savings partnership, reports over 274,000 accounts holding more than $50 million in college savings.
state_spotlights.qualifier: Reported by NYC Kids RISE; not included in New York's survey results.

credibility_facts.headline: 83% response rate
credibility_facts.approved_statement: The 2026 National 529 Survey drew responses from 43 states, including DC and the Private College 529 Plan, an 83 percent response rate.
credibility_facts.qualifier: Snapshot in time (2025 data); not directly comparable to the 2022 report.
